proposals.before: Princes Batu, Möngke, Ariq Böke, Sögtü, and Tachar, together with the generals Uriyangqadai, Sübetei, Temüder, and Yesu Buqa, assembled at Alagh Tagh, where Batu first moved to have him raised up.
proposals.after: Princes Batu, Möge, Ariq Böke, Sögtü, and Tachar, together with the generals Uriyangqadai, Sübetei, Temüder, and Yesu Buqa, assembled at Alagh Tagh, where Batu first moved to have him raised up.
proposals.reason: 中文作「木哥」(Möge), a distinct prince, not 蒙哥 (Möngke). Möngke is the subject being raised to the throne in this passage and cannot also be among the princes proposing him; the chapter writes his name 蒙哥 elsewhere.

proposals.before: The princes Batu, Möngke, Ariq Böke, Sögtü, and Tachar; the generals Uriyangqadai, Sübetei, Temüder, and Yesu Buqa — all met at Alagh Tagh, and Batu was the first to propose installing him.
proposals.after: The princes Batu, Möge, Ariq Böke, Sögtü, and Tachar; the generals Uriyangqadai, Sübetei, Temüder, and Yesu Buqa — all met at Alagh Tagh, and Batu was the first to propose installing him.
proposals.reason: 中文作「木哥」(Möge), a distinct prince, not 蒙哥 (Möngke). Möngke is the subject being raised to the throne in this passage and cannot also be among the princes proposing him; the chapter writes his name 蒙哥 elsewhere.

proposals.before: Möngke answered, "Who would dare defy Ögedei's command?
proposals.after: Möge answered, "Who would dare defy Ögedei's command?
proposals.reason: 中文作「木哥曰」: the speaker is Möge (木哥), not Möngke (蒙哥). Möngke is the person under discussion, addressed by the assembly; rendering 木哥 as Möngke collapses two distinct princes.

proposals.before: Möngke said: "Ögedei gave the command — who would dare disobey it?
proposals.after: Möge said: "Ögedei gave the command — who would dare disobey it?
proposals.reason: 中文作「木哥曰」: the speaker is Möge (木哥), not Möngke (蒙哥). Möngke is the person under discussion, addressed by the assembly; rendering 木哥 as Möngke collapses two distinct princes.

proposals.before: That year Qarachar was ordered to join Hong Wonyu in the campaign against Goryeo.
proposals.after: That year Qarachar was ordered to join Hong Wonyuan in the campaign against Goryeo.
proposals.reason: 洪福源 is rendered Hong Wonyuan in s0081; "Hong Wonyu" here drops the final syllable of 源 and splits one person into two spellings within the chapter.

proposals.before: That year Qarachar was reassigned to campaign against Goryeo jointly with Hong Wonyu.
proposals.after: That year Qarachar was reassigned to campaign against Goryeo jointly with Hong Wonyuan.
proposals.reason: 洪福源 is rendered Hong Wonyuan in s0081; "Hong Wonyu" here drops the final syllable of 源 and splits one person into two spellings within the chapter.

proposals.after: Uriyangqadai marched against the White Man and other tribes and broke them;
proposals.reason: 兀良合台 is transliterated Uriyangqadai elsewhere in this chapter (s0021, s0026, s0027, s0120); "Uryankhadai" is an inconsistent second spelling of the same commander.

proposals.reason: 兀良合台 is transliterated Uriyangqadai elsewhere in this chapter (s0021, s0026, s0027, s0120); "Uryankhadai" is an inconsistent second spelling of the same commander.

proposals.after: Quang Hựu sent his son-in-law with Annamese envoys bearing tribute; Uriyangqadai escorted them to the mobile court.

proposals.after: Quang Hựu sent his son-in-law with his countrymen bearing tribute to audience; Uriyangqadai escorted them to the imperial camp.

proposals.before: On rewu day in the tenth winter month the Emperor encamped at Baofeng.
proposals.after: On renwu day in the tenth winter month the Emperor encamped at Baofeng.
proposals.reason: 壬午 is romanized renwu; "rewu" drops the n of 壬 (rén) and is not a sexagenary day name.

proposals.before: On rewu day in the tenth month of winter the Emperor halted at Baofeng.
proposals.after: On renwu day in the tenth month of winter the Emperor halted at Baofeng.
proposals.reason: 壬午 is romanized renwu; "rewu" drops the n of 壬 (rén) and is not a sexagenary day name.

proposals.before: On rewu day in the twelfth month Yang Dayuan and Wang Tiange split their forces to strike Xiangru and neighboring counties.
proposals.after: On renwu day in the twelfth month Yang Dayuan and Wang Tiange split their forces to strike Xiangru and neighboring counties.
proposals.reason: 壬午 is romanized renwu; "rewu" drops the n of 壬 (rén) and is not a sexagenary day name.

proposals.before: On rewu day in the twelfth month Yang Dayuan led his troops with Wang Tiange to strike Xiangru and other counties separately.
proposals.after: On renwu day in the twelfth month Yang Dayuan led his troops with Wang Tiange to strike Xiangru and other counties separately.
proposals.reason: 壬午 is romanized renwu; "rewu" drops the n of 壬 (rén) and is not a sexagenary day name.

proposals.before: On yiyou day in the eleventh month the Emperor took command in person and opened the assault on Eding Fort.
proposals.after: On jiyou day in the eleventh month the Emperor took command in person and opened the assault on Eding Fort.
proposals.reason: 己酉 is romanized jiyou; "yiyou" would render 乙酉, a different day in the sexagenary cycle.

proposals.before: On yiyou day in the eleventh month the Emperor personally directed the army, first attacking Eding Fort.
proposals.after: On jiyou day in the eleventh month the Emperor personally directed the army, first attacking Eding Fort.
proposals.reason: 己酉 is romanized jiyou; "yiyou" would render 乙酉, a different day in the sexagenary cycle.

proposals.before: That month the Wang family prefect of Longzhou submitted.
proposals.after: That month Prefect Wang of Longzhou submitted.
proposals.reason: 龍州王知府 is "Prefect Wang of Longzhou" — surname 王 plus the office 知府 naming one官. "The Wang family prefect" reads 王 as a lineage rather than the man's surname.

proposals.before: In the ninth year (jiwei), on the new moon of the first spring month, the Emperor encamped north of Zhongguishan and held a great feast. He asked his princes, sons-in-law, and ministers, "We are deep in Song territory, and the summer heat is coming — can we endure it here?"
proposals.after: In the ninth year (jiwei), on the yisi day, the new moon of the first spring month, the Emperor encamped north of Zhongguishan and held a great feast. He asked his princes, sons-in-law, and ministers, "We are deep in Song territory, and the summer heat is coming — can we endure it here?"
proposals.reason: 正月乙巳朔 gives both the sexagenary day 乙巳 (yisi) and 朔 (new moon); the idiomatic rendering drops the day name that the literal rendering preserves.

proposals.before: On guiwei day, they attacked the Western Gate of the Garrison.
proposals.after: On guiwei day, they attacked Zhenxi Gate.
proposals.reason: 鎮西門 is the proper gate name Zhenxi Gate, not a garrison's western gate; the literal splits 鎮 as 'garrison' incorrectly.

proposals.before: In the sixth month, on dingsi day, Wang Tiange handpicked a force that climbed the cavalry redoubt on the outer wall by night and killed its commander and the men holding it.
proposals.after: In the sixth month, on dingsi day, Wang Tiange again handpicked a force that climbed the cavalry redoubt on the outer wall by night and killed its commander and the men holding it.
proposals.reason: Chinese 復選兵 means he selected troops again; the idiomatic English omits 復 'again'.

proposals.before: Henceforth he drafted every edict himself, revising each four times over before it went out.
proposals.after: Henceforth he drafted every edict himself, revising each several times before it went out.
proposals.reason: 更易數四 means revising several times (or three or four times), not strictly four times over.

decisions.reason: s0021 lists 諸王拔都木哥; 木哥 is Möge, not 蒙哥 (Möngke), who is the candidate being raised, so the proposed name change is required.
The literal likewise misreads 木哥 as Möngke; Möge matches the Chinese and keeps Möngke out of the proposing princes.
s0024 opens 木哥曰; the speaker is Möge, not Möngke, so the idiomatic attribution must change.
The literal repeats the same false speaker; 木哥曰 supports Möge said, not Möngke.
s0107 names 洪福源; Hong Wonyu drops 源 and conflicts with the chapter's Hong Wonyuan spelling, so the repair is correct.
The literal has the same truncated Hong Wonyu for 洪福源; Hong Wonyuan restores the full name.
s0121 names 兀良合台, already rendered Uriyangqadai elsewhere in this chapter; Uryankhadai is only an inconsistent second spelling.
The literal likewise needs Uriyangqadai for 兀良合台 to match the chapter's established spelling.
s0139 again has 兀良合台; replacing Uryankhadai with Uriyangqadai restores chapter-consistent naming.
The literal of s0139 repeats Uryankhadai for the same 兀良合台; Uriyangqadai is the correct repair.
s0146 names 兀良合台 escorting the tribute mission; Uriyangqadai matches the chapter spelling and Chinese.
The literal likewise mis-spells 兀良合台 as Uryankhadai; Uriyangqadai is the consistent correction.
s0175 dates the halt 冬十月壬午; 壬午 is renwu, and rewu is not a sexagenary day name.
The literal repeats rewu for 壬午; renwu is the accurate romanization.
s0197 opens 十二月壬午; renwu restores the correct sexagenary day, which rewu corrupts.
The literal of s0197 likewise needs renwu for 壬午 rather than the impossible rewu.
s0186 has 十一月己酉; 己酉 is jiyou, whereas yiyou would be 乙酉, a different day.
The literal repeats yiyou for 己酉; jiyou is the correct sexagenary reading.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 十一月己酉，帝督軍先攻鵝頂堡

decisions.reason: 龍州王知府 is Prefect Wang of Longzhou (surname 王 + office 知府), not a Wang-family prefect as a lineage office.
正月乙巳朔 supplies both the sexagenary day 乙巳 and 朔; restoring yisi day repairs the idiomatic omission without changing the rest.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 九年己未春正月乙巳朔

decisions.reason: 鎮西門 is the gate name Zhenxi Gate; reading 鎮 as 'garrison' invents a Western Gate of the Garrison the Chinese does not state.
汪田哥復選兵 includes 復 'again'; the proposed idiomatic restores that adverb omitted in the original.
更易數四 means revising several times (about three or four), not a fixed four times over; 'several times' matches the Chinese.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0007–r0012 show English Uryankhadai came only from inconsistent romanization of 兀良合台; Uriyangqadai is already claimed, so this alternate-name has no remaining source support.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0005 restores 洪福源 as Hong Wonyuan; the extracted Hong Wonyu alternate-name/textual-variant existed only from the truncated English spelling.
